original_text:
[SYNTHETIC NEWS: all entities, dates and events below are fictional]
Title: Bellmere board sets access rule for trial night gallery
Deck: A limited pilot will not open before the building inspection
The Bellmere Arts Board adopted an access rule on 11 May 2032 for a six-week trial beginning 1 June, subject to a passed building inspection. During the trial, the night gallery admits visitors aged 14 and older. Every admitted visitor must also hold a free timed ticket; a ticket does not waive the age rule. The rule concerns the night gallery alone and makes no claim about daytime admission.
The local access group called the pilot “a timid response to years of exclusion” and said the booking system disadvantages people without internet access. Board chair Mira Vale disputed that judgment, promising a staffed telephone booking line before opening. The promise is not evidence that the line is already operating.
The board has not measured trial attendance or estimated a permanent programme's costs. Its vote authorizes the pilot subject to the inspection; it does not approve permanent opening. A review is scheduled after the six weeks, and no extension is guaranteed.
Caption: A drawing of the planned gallery entrance, not a photograph of an operating night service.

sources.text: FICTIONAL STIPULATED PRIMARY RECORD S1. This author-created record is authoritative only inside this synthetic exercise, not real-world evidence. Bellmere Arts Board resolution, 11 May 2032: the six-week night-gallery pilot begins 1 June only if the building inspection is passed. Minimum visitor age is 16, inclusive. All admitted visitors also require a free timed ticket; tickets never override the minimum age. This resolution does not set daytime admission rules. It authorizes only this conditional pilot, not permanent opening. Attendance has not been measured, permanent-programme costs have not been estimated, and review after six weeks carries no guaranteed extension.
